clue.text: Experts — they can provide evidence for crime

definitions.meaning: a dab hand is a skilled person, so the plural word means experts

definitions.text: they can provide evidence for crime
definitions.meaning: old police slang for fingerprints, which help convict criminals

explanation.surface: A remark that specialists are the ones who can supply evidence in a criminal case.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: skilled people (from 'dab hand') and slang for fingerprints left at a crime scene.

clue.text: Dejected actors in county of Northern Ireland

parts.note: Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland
the cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A troupe of performers touring Northern Ireland are feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is in Northern Ireland; the county comes first in the answer even though the actors come first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone downcast has low spirits, a close synonym for being dejected.

clue.text: Painful sore makes one get agitated

definitions.meaning: an inflamed pus-filled swelling on the skin
to seethe with anger or excitement, as a liquid bubbles in heat

explanation.surface: A sore spot that hurts would make anyone irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a skin abscess, and the verb for seething with rage or excitement.

clue.text: Female star in cabin humourless in expression

indicators.note: in places the female star within the cabin, so those letters sit inside the word for cabin

parts.note: a pod is a small compartment or cabin, as on a cable car or spacecraft
an ace is a star performer

explanation.surface: A leading actress shut in a cabin wears a stony face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' reads as a celebrity but here means an expert, an ace; 'cabin' is the small enclosed kind, a pod.
explanation.definitionFit: Po-faced describes a solemn, disapproving look, a face without humour.

clue.text: Lots of work around hospital department

indicators.note: around means the word for work wraps itself about the hospital department

parts.note: to ply is to work steadily at a trade
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: There is a great deal of work in and around one hospital unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' is a verb here, as in plying a trade, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A plentiful supply means lots, an abundance of something.

clue.text: Showed an interest in legal process and did likewise

parts.note: to follow a subject, team or story is to keep up an interest in it
a suit is a lawsuit, a case brought in court

explanation.surface: Someone kept an eye on a court case and then copied what others did.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from card games, where one plays the same suit as the lead, hence imitating another's action.

clue.text: Farm animal falls over in flowering plants

parts.note: a cow is a typical farm animal
slips means loses footing and tumbles

explanation.surface: A cow loses its footing and tumbles into the wild flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowslips are yellow spring wildflowers of the primrose family, common in meadows.

clue.text: Challenge accepted by one radical rising up

indicators.note: rising up says the hidden letters are read backwards, as this is a down clue
accepted by means the letters are taken in, held within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A provocation is taken up by a revolutionary standing up to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Challenge accepted' as the definition, but 'accepted by' is the signal that the letters sit inside 'one radical'; the definition is 'Challenge' alone. ERAD is then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dare is a challenge to do something bold, as a noun meaning a provocation.

clue.text: German soldier spreading most terror with op

indicators.note: spreading means the letters are scattered and laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: An enemy fighter sows maximum fear during a military operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormtroopers were the shock troops of the German army in the First World War, later the Nazi SA.

clue.text: Discloser of scandal troubling to well-wisher — British involved

indicators.note: troubling suggests the letters are stirred up and disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: An exposé of wrongdoing is distressing to a supporter of the British.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' says the B is mixed in with the letters of TO WELL-WISHER before 'troubling' rearranges them all.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistle-blower is an insider who exposes wrongdoing, so a revealer of scandal.

clue.text: Girl spends hour in routine procedure

indicators.note: spends means she uses up and so loses the letter for hour

explanation.surface: A young woman passes an hour stuck in her daily grind.
explanation.definitionFit: A rut is a fixed, dull pattern of behaviour, a habitual routine.

clue.text: Idiot in the morning in Indian location

parts.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A fool turns up somewhere in India one morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a state in north-east India, famous for its tea.

clue.text: Finally teach class or upset those in it?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and so jumbled into another order
finally picks out the closing letter of the word teach

explanation.surface: A teacher's last word to a class: settle down, or be overturned?
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the class, so the definition leans on the rest of the clue; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils in a class are scholars, an old word for schoolchildren.

clue.text: After end of day canvas shelter is wide open

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word day

parts.note: an awning is a canvas sheet stretched over a shopfront or window

explanation.surface: At dusk the tent flap is left gaping.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawning gap or chasm is one gaping wide.

clue.text: Good and mature, but unable to go up in the world?

definitions.meaning: a well-balanced, sensible person with feet on the ground

definitions.text: unable to go up in the world?
definitions.meaning: an aircraft or pilot kept from flying is unable to take to the air; the phrase pretends to mean social climbing

explanation.surface: A sensible adult who nonetheless cannot get ahead in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go up in the world' usually means to rise socially; here it means literally take off.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: emotionally stable and sensible, and of an aircraft barred from flying.

clue.text: Garments flogged in this street — 50% off

indicators.note: flogged suggests the letters are beaten into a new shape
50% off keeps only the first half of the word street

explanation.surface: Clothes sold cheaply on a market street at half price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogged' is British slang for sold, but here it signals the rearrangement of THIS plus STR.
explanation.definitionFit: These are short-sleeved collarless tops, a casual kind of clothing.

clue.text: Saracens initially given 50/50 chance in game of rugby

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of Saracens

parts.note: evens are betting odds of one to one, an equal chance

explanation.surface: Saracens, a London rugby club, given an even chance in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is the seven-a-side version of rugby union.

clue.text: Daughter is taking care of entertainment event

parts.note: c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: A daughter looks after the arrangements for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a dance party with recorded music, a social event.

clue.text: See some of them swimming in German river

indicators.note: some of says only part of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Look at some people bathing in a river in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ems is a river in north-west Germany flowing into the North Sea.

clue.text: Turning up, bishop gets to express satisfaction audibly

indicators.note: turning says the word up is flipped round, read in reverse

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop rises from his seat, pleased with himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat purrs with a low hum when content, so it is a contented sound.

clue.text: Procedure observed in latest epistle

indicators.note: observed in means the letters can be seen inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A method spelled out in the newest letter from an apostle.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is one stage or measure in a process, a procedure taken.

clue.text: Canute, a dipper sadly not respected

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are in disorder

explanation.surface: King Canute, who sat in the tide getting a dunking, was sadly underrated.
explanation.walkthrough: Canute was the English king said to have shown the sea would not obey him.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unappreciated is not valued or given due regard.

clue.text: Gives new order to holiday towns?

definitions.meaning: to sort again, arranging items afresh
seaside or ski places where people go on holiday

explanation.surface: Someone rearranges the list of holiday destinations.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first sense as RE-SORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: sorts again, and places such as seaside towns visited by holidaymakers.

clue.text: Copied a page written by editor

explanation.surface: A page by the editor was plagiarised.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape is to mimic or imitate, so aped is a past-tense synonym.
